title: Halifax JD259 Memorial, Mechelen-Leest
location_name: Leest, Mechelen municipality, Antwerp province, Belgium
cause_of_loss: Shot down by Oblt Wilhelm Telge, Stab II./NJG 1, his 7th Abschuss, at 02:30 on 22 June 1943 over Belgium
memorial_details: Memorial stone with plaque at the crash site in Leest, Mechelen. Origin and current custodian of the memorial not confirmed — the 158 Squadron Association notes: 'It is unknown at this time who is responsible for the erection of this memorial.'
crew_summary: All seven killed. Six buried Schoonselhof Cemetery, Antwerp. P/O Maund initially buried near crash site; later reinterred Schoonselhof. The aircraft struck high-tension cables just before touchdown during a forced landing attempt.
narrative:
JD259 was one of 557 aircraft detailed against Mülheim on the night of 21/22 June 1943, part of the Battle of the Ruhr. The aircraft departed Lissett and bombed the target. On the return, Oblt Wilhelm Telge of Stab II./NJG 1 intercepted it over Belgium for his seventh confirmed kill at 02:30.

The pilot — F/Sgt Leonard Cavanagh, a 20-year-old Australian — made what the 158 Squadron Association describes as a very brave attempt to crash-land the bomber. Just before touchdown the aircraft struck high-tension cables and exploded, scattering wreckage across fields near the railway at Leest. All seven men died. P/O Maund was buried initially where he fell; the other six were taken to Schoonselhof Cemetery in Antwerp. After the war Maund was reinterred alongside his crewmates.

F/Sgt Cavanagh, from Western Australia, is the named focus of the 158 Squadron Association's memorial page — a common pattern in which one crew member, often through family connection or nationality, becomes the focal point for commemoration while the memorial itself honours the whole crew.

crew.name: R.A.C. Maund
crew.fate_detail: Initially buried near crash site; later reinterred Schoonselhof Cemetery.

sources.title: 158 Squadron Association — Memorial to Crew of Halifax JD259

contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register
community_connection: 158 Squadron Association maintains a memorial page for the crew at https://www.158squadron.co.uk/memorials/cavanagh. The local Belgian community at Leest/Mechelen maintains the crash-site memorial, though the erecting organisation is unknown per the 158 Squadron Association.
